# Conversation

**Package** `telividb.conversation.v1`

## Services

### `Conversations`

Manages conversations and the messages within them.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `GetConversation` | `GetConversationRequest` | `Conversation` | Retrieves a single conversation. |
| `ListConversations` | `ListConversationsRequest` | `ListConversationsResponse` | Lists conversations, filtered by space, session or project. |
| `MoveConversation` | `MoveConversationRequest` | `MoveConversationResponse` | Moves a conversation into another session, and so into another space. The resource name does not change, which is the entire reason session and space are fields rather than path segments: a move that renamed the conversation would invalidate every edge endpoint, archive entry and citation that refers to it. The move itself is a metadata transaction. No vector data is touched, because membership is never written into a segment — which is what makes this cheap rather than a rewrite. |
| `SuppressConversation` | `SuppressConversationRequest` | `Conversation` | Excludes a conversation from ordinary recall without deleting it. Suppression is a third state, distinct from deletion and from a policy denial: the content is retained, its owner can still reach it deliberately, and traversal stops at it rather than ranking it low. Its existence stays visible to a caller assembling context — so an agent knows what not to raise — while the rendered answer must not surface it, because delivering the reminder is the harm suppression was asked for. A separate method rather than a field update so that setting it is its own audit entry. Only the owner may call it; a classifier may propose suppression and may never apply or lift it. |
| `UnsuppressConversation` | `UnsuppressConversationRequest` | `Conversation` | Returns a suppressed conversation to ordinary recall. |
| `DeleteConversation` | `DeleteConversationRequest` | `Conversation` | Soft-deletes a conversation and the messages beneath it. |
| `CreateMessage` | `CreateMessageRequest` | `Message` | Appends a message, branching where the request says to. Embedding happens server-side through the one inference server, so the model that produced a field's vectors is a property of the server rather than of whichever client wrote them. System and developer turns are stored without being encoded. |

| `ListMessages` | `ListMessagesRequest` | `ListMessagesResponse` | Lists the messages of a conversation, every branch by default. |

A call and its result are one resource here, and returning them inside the message stream would rebuild the two-message split this model exists to avoid. |

The coarse tier of retrieval: a search runs against these first and expands into messages only where it needs to. Each carries the watermark it reached and whether its subject has changed since, so a stale summary is served honestly rather than passed off as current. |

## Messages

### `Conversation`

An exchange of messages, and the unit that moves between spaces.  Named under its organization and nothing else. Session, space and project are fields rather than path segments because a conversation moves between them, and a move that renamed the resource would break every stored edge endpoint, every archived reference and every citation in an assembled answer — external names are the only portable identity there is.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the conversation. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | Human-readable name. |
| `session` | `string` | 3 |  | Session this conversation was recorded in. |
| `head` | `string` | 4 |  | The message currently at the end of the active branch. Messages form a directed acyclic graph rather than a chain: regenerating a reply or editing and resubmitting creates a sibling, so a message may have several children. This names which leaf the default retrieval path ends at; other branches remain reachable but are not followed by default. |
| `suppressed` | `bool` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether this conversation is excluded from ordinary recall. Suppression retains the content and leaves it reachable to its owner deliberately, while stopping traversal and keeping it out of assembled context. It is a recall preference over the owner's own memory, never an access-control mechanism — a principal denied by policy is denied whether this is set or not. |
| `message_count` | `int32` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Messages on the active branch. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the conversation was created. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the conversation was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the conversation was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted conversation is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 11 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `ContentRef`

A pointer to the bytes a message was derived from.  Declared here rather than imported: a package that reached into a shared one would couple its versioning to that package's, which AIP-215 forbids.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uri` | `string` | 1 | `OPTIONAL` | Location of the source, such as `file://`, `s3://` or `https://`. |
| `sha256` | `bytes` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | SHA-256 digest of the referenced bytes. What detects that a source changed and anything derived from it — an embedding, a summary — is now stale. |
| `inline_text` | `string` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | Source text, inlined when small enough to keep the message re-embeddable. Without a reachable source, content is locked to the model that first encoded it. |

### `Message`

One turn in a conversation.  Modelled on the OpenAI chat message because that vocabulary is universal and round-trips into every agent framework — but *projected* to that shape at the boundary rather than stored in it. That format is not a specification and it churns, and a stored field number is permanent.  A message is one resource and several stored points: long content is chunked for the encoder, and each chunk records which part of this message it covers.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the message. |
| `role` | `Role` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Who produced this turn. |
| `parent` | `string` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | The message this one replies to. A message may have several children: regenerating or editing branches the conversation rather than replacing what was there. Discarded branches are retained, because an abandoned attempt is evidence about what was tried. Holds a message resource name, but deliberately carries no `resource_reference`. That annotation describes an edge in the graph of resource *types*, and a self-edge is a cycle there — which AIP-121 refuses, because a cycle between resource types has no consistent creation order. The refusal is right about types and wrong about instances: these form a tree, and a parent always exists before its child. Annotating it anyway would be asserting something false about the type graph to describe something true about the data, so the field is a plain name instead. The same shape Google's own tree-structured resources use. Set once, when the message is appended, and never rewritten — branching adds a sibling rather than reparenting anything. |
| `content` | `string` | 4 | `OPTIONAL` | Textual content of the turn. |
| `content_ref` | `ContentRef` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Reference to the bytes this message was derived from, for content too large to inline. |
| `embedded` | `bool` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether this message contributed vectors to the index. Not every turn is embedded. System and developer content is boilerplate that ranks against real content and degrades retrieval, so it is stored and searchable by filter without being encoded. |
| `occur_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OPTIONAL` | When the turn occurred. Time is a ranking term here rather than only a filter: "what did we discuss last Tuesday" has a weak semantic signal and a strong temporal one. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the message was recorded. |
| `etag` | `string` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `Summary`

A condensation of what a region of memory contains.  Summaries form the coarse tier of a two-tier retrieval: a search runs against them first, then expands along the edges recording what each one covers. That is the same coarse-to-fine shape the vector path already uses when a quantized scan narrows the field before a full-precision rerank, applied at the semantic layer instead of the numeric one.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the summary. |
| `level` | `Level` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Which layer of the tree this summarizes. Declared rather than inferred from ordering. "Newest first" sorts within a level; it does not distinguish a conversation summary from a space one, and a series that relies on recency to tell them apart cannot answer "summarize this space" without re-deriving which entries were which. |
| `subject` | `string` | 3 | `REQUIRED` | The resource this summary is attached to. |
| `content` | `string` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The summary text. |
| `coverage_end_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | How far into the subject this summary reached — its watermark. A summary is derived data and goes stale: a new message extends past it, a branch changes which messages are on the active path, and a conversation moving between spaces invalidates summaries on both sides. The watermark This is what makes staleness detectable rather than silent. |
| `stale` | `bool` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether the subject has changed since this summary was generated. A stale summary is still served, marked, with its watermark — an old summary plus an honest marker is more useful than a gap, and serving one as current is the failure with no symptom. |
| `model_digest` | `string` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Digest of the model that produced this summary. The identity, not a label. A summary that turns out to be wrong is traced to the run that produced it and re-derived. |
| `inherited_protection` | `string` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Strictest protection among the sources this summary covers. A summary of protected content is protected content: it is derived from the text and leaks it regardless of what guards the original. A summary spanning several spaces takes the most restrictive protection of any of them, never the average and never the destination's — otherwise summarizing across a boundary would be a declassification channel. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the summary was generated. |

### `ToolInvocation`

One tool call and the result it returned.  A call and its result are one event with one lifetime and one set of permissions. The OpenAI wire format splits them across two messages — the call embedded in an assistant turn, the result as a separate turn keyed by `tool_call_id` — but that split is an artefact of JSON having no way to express a cross-message reference. Here the reference is an edge, and the two-message form is reconstructed deterministically on the way out.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the invocation. |
| `caller` | `string` | 2 |  | The message that triggered this call. |
| `call_id` | `string` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | Identifier carried by the originating format, preserved for round-trip. Stored so a conversation exported back to an OpenAI-shaped transcript reproduces the same `tool_call_id` it arrived with. Never used internally to resolve the relationship — an edge does that. |
| `tool` | `string` | 4 | `REQUIRED` | The tool that was called. |
| `input` | `string` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Arguments the tool was called with, JSON-encoded. A string rather than a `Struct`, and that is a deliberate narrowing. The shape is whatever the tool's own JSON Schema declares, so it is not knowable here — and a dynamically typed value has no equivalent in a flat format: rendering it degrades to a JSON string in FlatBuffers and to an opaque pointer in Cap'n Proto that no generated accessor can read. Storing what it actually is keeps every projection of this schema honest. Never embedded. JSON ranks against real content; the useful operations are filtering on `tool` and `mcp_server`, not searching arguments by similarity. |
| `result` | `ContentRef` | 6 | `OPTIONAL` | What the tool returned. Inlined when small; a reference when large, because a result can be megabytes and blobs stay outside the database. |
| `state` | `State` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether the call succeeded. |
| `mcp_server` | `string` | 8 |  | The MCP server that produced this result. Recorded on every invocation whether or not the result was embedded, because provenance is what lets retrieval distinguish something a person said from something a third-party server said. Without it those rank equally as memory, and text returned by a server is written by whoever runs that server. |
| `embedded` | `bool` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether the result contributed vectors to the index. False unless the originating server is explicitly marked embeddable. A result that is embedded becomes retrievable memory and can later be assembled into a context window, so an untrusted one is a persistent injection surface rather than a one-time one. The default withholds. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the call was made. |
